topic-096-a-definition-of-continual-rein.evolution: The representatives range from learning utilities and macro-actions to reward-free behavior spaces and episodic feedback. Recent preference-learning theory compares explicit reward modeling with direct policy optimization, showing that relative performance depends on model misspecification and available samples.
openQuestions: Which reward representations support useful adaptation to genuinely new tasks?
How should reward-model and policy capacity be matched when learning from limited preferences?
topic-096-a-definition-of-continual-rein.overview: This topic asks how rewards should be represented, inferred, or supplied to learning agents. Papers explore intrinsic rewards, reward machines, successor-style representations, inverse reinforcement learning, and preference-based optimization. A representative forward-backward representation learns long-range state–action relationships without rewards, then converts a newly specified reward into a policy without additional planning.
topic-096-a-definition-of-continual-rein.title: Reward Representations and Preference-Based Policy Learning
topic-096-a-definition-of-continual-rein.whyItMatters: An agent's behavior depends on both its learning algorithm and the way its objective is expressed. Reusable dynamics representations can support many tasks, while learned reward models introduce capacity and statistical assumptions that affect which preferences the final policy can satisfy.

topic-097-learning-opinions-in-social-ne.evolution: The representatives develop diffusion-network inference and scalable influence estimation, followed by sample-based learning and community-aware influence methods. Recent work addresses online feedback and simulation transfer. Related latent-network theory examines how choosing an incorrect embedding dimension affects structural estimation.
openQuestions: When do accurate marginal predictions suffice for reliable interventions?
How can influence methods remain effective when network structure and propagation mechanisms change together?
topic-097-learning-opinions-in-social-ne.overview: Network diffusion models describe how activity or information spreads between connected entities. This topic studies learning those dynamics from partial observations, estimating influence, and selecting interventions. A representative method uses dynamic message passing to learn an effective cascade model from limited activation-time information, optimizing the quality of predictions needed for downstream control.
topic-097-learning-opinions-in-social-ne.title: Network Diffusion, Influence, and Latent Structure
topic-097-learning-opinions-in-social-ne.whyItMatters: Incomplete observations make the underlying network and spreading process uncertain. A model useful for forecasting or intervention must account for that uncertainty rather than assuming that observed cascades directly reveal every connection or transmission probability.

topic-098-a-distributed-variational-infe.evolution: Earlier representatives develop sparse Gaussian processes and dynamical applications. Later work automates variational inference and challenges restrictive mean-field assumptions. Recent methods combine neural embeddings, inducing-kernel approximations, and stochastic inference to handle richer random fields or very large output spaces.
openQuestions: How can approximation error be diagnosed separately from a poorly chosen kernel?
Which scalable constructions retain calibrated uncertainty when outputs or inputs move beyond the training distribution?
topic-098-a-distributed-variational-infe.overview: Gaussian processes provide distributions over functions, but exact inference can become expensive or intractable in large or complex models. This cluster develops sparse representations, variational approximations, deep constructions, and multi-output dependencies. A representative black-box variational approach estimates objectives efficiently while allowing likelihoods that would otherwise require specialized inference derivations.
topic-098-a-distributed-variational-infe.title: Scalable Inference for Structured Gaussian Processes
topic-098-a-distributed-variational-infe.whyItMatters: Approximation determines whether a probabilistic model remains useful at realistic scale. Saving computation should be assessed alongside retained dependencies and predictive uncertainty, especially when many outputs or hierarchical layers interact.

topic-099-a-closer-look-at-few-shot-clas.evolution: The representatives begin with semantic output codes and compositional one-shot learning. Later work examines dataset generalization, unlabeled target data, and online adapters. Recent papers analyze synthetic-data benefits, noisy few-shot settings, and methods for correcting seen-class bias during generalized zero-shot inference.
openQuestions: When does synthetic augmentation add information instead of reinforcing initial errors?
How can unseen-class calibration be evaluated without exploiting unavailable test labels?
topic-099-a-closer-look-at-few-shot-clas.overview: Few-shot learning adapts from very small labeled datasets, while zero-shot learning relies on transferable semantic information for unseen categories. This topic includes synthetic augmentation, cross-domain transfer, vision-language adaptation, and calibration between seen and unseen classes. One representative method tunes a language model to generate label-discriminative training examples, then uses them to augment scarce supervision.
topic-099-a-closer-look-at-few-shot-clas.title: Few-Shot and Zero-Shot Generalization
topic-099-a-closer-look-at-few-shot-clas.whyItMatters: Limited labels make models sensitive to sampling noise, domain mismatch, and biases inherited from pretraining. Additional generated data or semantic prototypes help only when they preserve the distinctions needed by the new task.

topic-100-3-in-1-2d-rotary-adaptation-fo.evolution: The representatives include earlier memory-based and abstract reasoning alongside recent language-model methods. Newer papers focus on adaptive stopping, difficulty estimation, parallel reasoning, instruction-following failures, and attention-head-aware cache compression. Together they investigate where computation contributes to reasoning quality.
openQuestions: How can a model predict the marginal value of further reasoning?
Which reasoning dependencies can be parallelized or compressed without introducing difficult-to-detect errors?
topic-100-3-in-1-2d-rotary-adaptation-fo.overview: Reasoning models can spend substantial computation on long intermediate sequences. This topic studies when to continue reasoning, how to organize independent subproblems, and which internal state must be retained. A representative framework trains models to interleave planning with parallel execution, reducing sequential work while preserving task performance in its evaluations.
topic-100-3-in-1-2d-rotary-adaptation-fo.title: Adaptive Reasoning Computation and Inference Control
topic-100-3-in-1-2d-rotary-adaptation-fo.whyItMatters: Longer reasoning is not always more useful, and unnecessary steps increase latency and memory use. Effective control must estimate whether extra computation is likely to improve the answer without prematurely stopping difficult problems or disrupting essential dependencies.

topic-101-characterizing-the-gap-between.evolution: Early representatives establish convergence and stable approximation in dynamic programming. Later work develops linear and doubly robust off-policy methods. Recent research connects average and discounted learning and studies sequence-level trust regions for long-horizon language-model reinforcement learning, where small local discrepancies can accumulate.
openQuestions: How can useful off-policy data be retained without unstable corrections?
Which stability guarantees survive nonlinear approximation and changing data-collection policies?
topic-101-characterizing-the-gap-between.overview: Off-policy learning uses experience collected by one policy to evaluate or improve another. This cluster studies temporal-difference updates, actor–critic algorithms, importance corrections, variance reduction, and function approximation. A representative recognizer method filters actions to create related target policies with lower-variance corrections and convergence guarantees in specified approximation settings.
topic-101-characterizing-the-gap-between.title: Off-Policy Evaluation and Stable Temporal-Difference Learning
topic-101-characterizing-the-gap-between.whyItMatters: Reusing data can make learning much more efficient, but mismatches between collection and target policies can amplify variance or destabilize updates. The same issue appears in distributed training when a rollout policy differs from the policy being optimized.

topic-102-chameleon-adapting-to-peer-ima.evolution: The representatives range from malicious learning and intrusion detection to modern poisoning and backdoor defenses. Recent work adds continual-learning guarantees and studies unlearning's collateral damage and relearning attacks. These directions broaden evaluation from immediate removal toward the durability and selectivity of a defense.
openQuestions: How can defenses be tested against adaptive attacks under realistic data access?
What evidence distinguishes durable unlearning from temporary suppression of an accessible representation?
topic-102-chameleon-adapting-to-peer-ima.overview: This topic studies malicious changes to training data and methods for removing or neutralizing unwanted learned behavior. Backdoor attacks associate a hidden trigger with an attacker-chosen output; defenses examine suspicious samples, training dynamics, or controlled interventions. Related unlearning work asks whether designated knowledge can be removed without damaging retained capabilities.
topic-102-chameleon-adapting-to-peer-ima.title: Training-Data Poisoning, Backdoors, and Reliable Unlearning
topic-102-chameleon-adapting-to-peer-ima.whyItMatters: A model may perform well on ordinary tests while containing targeted vulnerabilities. Defense evaluation therefore needs to examine attacker adaptation, clean-task utility, and whether supposedly removed behavior can be recovered through subsequent learning.

topic-103-poem-out-of-distribution-detec.evolution: The representatives develop semantic and density-based detectors before exploring feature geometry and distributional augmentation. Recent work extends detection to tabular foundation models and graphs, where changes in node attributes and connectivity introduce distinct sources of unfamiliarity.
openQuestions: How can evaluations cover shifts that differ substantially from training-time outliers?
Which detection signals remain reliable while preserving accuracy on difficult but legitimate inputs?
topic-103-poem-out-of-distribution-detec.overview: Out-of-distribution detection asks whether an input lies outside the conditions a model was trained to handle. These papers use likelihood ratios, nearest neighbors, gradients, logits, and information decomposition to identify unfamiliar examples. A representative training approach accounts for the discrepancy between auxiliary outliers available during training and the unseen outliers encountered later.
topic-103-poem-out-of-distribution-detec.title: Out-of-Distribution Detection and Open-World Reliability
topic-103-poem-out-of-distribution-detec.whyItMatters: A classifier can be confident on inputs for which its labels or learned relationships no longer apply. Reliable detection can support abstention or further review, but performance on one curated outlier set does not establish broad open-world reliability.
